source_name: MNB_Hungary official X/Twitter account (conference speaker announcements)
why_relevant: MNB announces named keynote speakers and their titles on X weeks before the website programme is finalised; earliest public signal of who will represent which institution.

source_name: NFSZ – Nemzeti Foglalkoztatási Szolgálat: Csoportos létszámleépítések bejelentése
source_subtype: government employment authority / statutory notification portal
why_relevant: Statutory channel through which Hungarian employers (banks included) must notify intended and decided collective redundancies (csoportos letszamcsokkentes) to the government employment authority; describes the ESTAT electronic notification system and which kormanyhivatal receives the filing. This is the legally-compelled negative-signal pipeline for A5.

source_name: NFSZ – Munkaerőpiaci statisztikák, elemzések
why_relevant: Hub for NFSZ labour-market statistics and interactive graphics; the series used by Hungarian media (e.g. HR Portal) when reporting how many workers are affected by collective redundancies nationally and by sector.

source_name: NFSZ – Bértámogatás a csoportos létszámleépítés elkerülésére (tájékoztató)
why_relevant: Subsidy scheme documentation for avoiding/mitigating collective redundancies; the existence of applications and scheme rules signals which employers are in distress and defines the administrative vocabulary used in filings.

source_name: BBDSZ – Bankok és Biztosítók Dolgozóinak Szakszervezeti Szövetsége (Federation of Unions of the Finance Sector)
why_relevant: The sectoral union federation for Hungarian banking and insurance workers; the counterparty in collective agreement negotiations and the actor legally consulted in collective redundancy procedures. Its statements and news are the primary union-side record of restructuring disputes.

source_name: BDDSZ – Kollektív Szerződés resources (union collective-agreement library)
why_relevant: Publishes collective-agreement guidance and model texts (including a downloadable KSZ minta). Useful as a template/benchmark for interpreting bank-level collective agreements and works-council consultation duties; note this is BDDSZ, a different union from BBDSZ — an easily-confused near-homograph acronym.

source_name: Munkástanácsok Országos Szövetsége – finance-sector union news
why_relevant: National union confederation (~100 affiliates) that admitted the newly formed UniCredit Bank Hungary Zrt. Vallalatcsoport Szakszervezete and published the immediate-effect dismissal of that union's president in April 2026. Highest-signal, most current union-side reporting on Hungarian bank labour conflict found in this cell.

source_name: Szakszervezetek.hu – Hungarian trade union news portal
why_relevant: Cross-confederation union news aggregator (ESZT, LIGA, MASZSZ, Munkastanacsok, SZEF joint statements); good pointer layer for discovering which finance-sector unions exist and when sectoral disputes escalate. Also hosts a union database in its archive.

source_name: LIGA Szakszervezetek (Liganet)
why_relevant: One of the confederations at the national wage-bargaining table (VKF); its positions shape the sectoral wage/collective-agreement backdrop against which bank restructuring is negotiated.

source_name: Eurofound – European Restructuring Monitor (ERM) restructuring events database
why_relevant: Case-level, structured factsheets on large restructuring events (job losses, internal restructuring, closures) per country and sector since 2002, including Hungarian bank cases (K&H Bank Hungary internal restructuring; MKB Bank reorganisation; Raiffeisen and Erste Hungary staff cuts). The single best cross-border structured negative-signal dataset for this cell.

source_name: Eurofound – ERM restructuring-related legislation database
source_subtype: EU agency legal database / methodology doc
why_relevant: Documents the Hungarian legal framework for collective redundancy (notification thresholds, consultation duties) alongside other member states — needed to interpret whether a given bank cut is legally notifiable and therefore documentarily traceable.

source_name: UNI Europa – Finance sector
why_relevant: European federation of ~100 finance-sector unions; useful pointer to identify which Hungarian bank unions are internationally affiliated, and a channel where cross-border restructuring (e.g. group-level integration at Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit) is contested and documented.

source_name: MNB Aranykönyv (Golden Book) – supervised institutions' individual data, incl. branch and headcount series
why_relevant: Central bank supervisory dataset with per-institution annual figures (2003 onward) in interactive and xlsx form — the authoritative quantitative baseline for detecting shrinking branch networks and headcount at named Hungarian credit institutions, independent of what banks announce.

source_name: KSH STADAT – employment and earnings by national economy branch (K: financial and insurance activities)
why_relevant: Official statistics office series for headcount (alkalmazasban allok) and earnings by NACE branch K, with financial/insurance coverage extended from 2021 under EU regulation. Gives the sector-wide employment trend against which individual bank cuts can be sized.

source_name: HR Portál – létszámleépítés / elbocsátás tag streams and periodic mass-layoff round-ups
why_relevant: Hungarian HR trade press that periodically compiles NFSZ collective-redundancy data into named round-ups and covers finance-sector labour conflicts (it reported the UniCredit union president's dismissal in April 2026). Effectively a secondary index over the NFSZ filings that are otherwise hard to obtain case-by-case.

source_name: mfor.hu / Privátbankár branch-network and headcount survey series
why_relevant: Runs a recurring bank-by-bank survey of branch counts and employee numbers, including the important counter-signal that branch closures in Hungary have NOT been accompanied by headcount reduction (sector employment rose past 40,500 by March 2026). Directly tests the assumption behind this cell.

source_name: Pénzcentrum – bank branch closure coverage
why_relevant: Consumer-finance outlet that reports named branch closure waves (MBH's post-merger network cuts: ~60 branches in one year, 360+ since the Budapest Bank/MKB/Takarekbank merger). Useful for dating and localising closures.

source_name: money.hu tudástár – banking network statistics reporting
why_relevant: Publishes quantified branch-count time series (1401 branches at start of 2025 → 1300 at year end → 1268 at 31 March 2026), i.e. a ready-made derived indicator of network contraction with quarterly granularity.

source_name: MBH Bank – Közzétételek (regulatory disclosures) and MBH bond programme base prospectus
why_relevant: Issuer-mandated disclosures from the merged MBH group — the single largest source of post-merger integration events in Hungary. Prospectus supplements carry structural facts (e.g. MBH Befektetési Bank leaving the Integrációs Szervezet on 1 Jan 2026; MBH Duna Bank taking over the integration business-steering role) that precede and explain workforce and branch consolidation.

source_name: Index.hu – gazdaság / belföld banking labour and operations coverage
why_relevant: Mainstream outlet that covers finance-sector unionisation and bank operational disruptions; carried both the historical 'finance workers unionise' story and the 2026 UniCredit union-president dismissal with named counsel and the legal issue in dispute (business-secret rules).

source_name: Céginfo.hu – union and employer legal-entity registry records
why_relevant: Registry lookup confirming legal existence, registration number and officers of finance-sector unions (here BBDSZ) and of bank entities. Lets you separate live actors from defunct ones and resolve name/acronym collisions before attributing statements.

source_name: Employment-law practitioner commentary on collective redundancy (arsboni, drujvary, Jogkövető iratminták)
why_relevant: Explains the Hungarian thresholds, timelines, works-council (üzemi tanács) consultation duty and the mandatory authority notification — necessary to know exactly what documentary artefacts a given bank cut must generate and when. Jogkövető publishes the actual works-council notification template.

source_name: EY Hungary – pay transparency and worker-representative consultation guidance
why_relevant: Maps the new/expanding consultation obligations toward worker representatives in Hungary — an emerging source of disclosure duties that will generate additional documentary traces around restructuring and pay in banks.

source_name: Portfolio.hu / Economx – national wage bargaining (VKF) and banking sector coverage
why_relevant: Tracks the national wage bargain (VKF) rounds that set the envelope for bank-level collective agreements; Economx reported new bargaining rounds starting September 2026. Portfolio also covers bank governance/conduct and restructuring.

source_name: Céginformációs Szolgálat – beszámoló-állomány értékesítése (bulk filing dataset)
why_relevant: Official route to obtain the whole filed-accounts corpus (or grouped queries over it) rather than scraping company-by-company. This is the scalable path to sector-wide headcount time series for banks and payment firms.

source_name: Céginformációs Szolgálat – Cégfigyelés (official company-monitoring service)
why_relevant: Official subscription alerting on Cégközlöny entries and submissions for monitored companies — turns the gazette from a polling problem into a push feed for a fixed watchlist of banks and payment institutions.

source_name: OTP Bank Nyrt. – Éves jelentés / Integrált éves jelentés (IR)
why_relevant: Largest HU bank's integrated annual report: igazgatóság and felügyelőbizottság rosters with professional bios, group headcount ('záró létszám'/average headcount) by country and segment, and organizational structure. Year-over-year diffs of these tables reveal both leadership churn and restructuring.

source_name: OTP Bank – Közgyűlési dokumentumok és határozatok (AGM documents)
why_relevant: AGM proposals and resolutions state elections, re-elections and terminations of igazgatóság/felügyelőbizottság/audit bizottság members with exact effective dates — the crispest primary record of board-level leadership moves, published before annual reports.
